name: Objection Drilldown
description: Weekly objection intelligence report, as an Attention agent-builder flow: schedule -> askAttention (pull the week's calls, classify objections, score handling, extract rebuttals, compare to last week) -> post to a channel. CONFIRM against your builder before import: the schema this was modeled on is a per-call agent, so three things here are best-effort and flagged in objection-drilldown.md -> Build notes: (1) the @activepieces/piece-schedule trigger + version, (2) the askAttention context scope for a cross-call query, (3) the Slack channel-post action name. Set connections and the placeholder ids (<...>) on import.

nextAction.name: analyze_objections
nextAction.displayName: Classify objections, score handling, extract rebuttals, compare to last week

input.prompt: You are the Objection Drilldown agent. (1) Pull every team call from the last 7 days. If fewer than 5 calls, note the small sample and that trends may not be meaningful. (2) Classify every prospect objection into ONE category from: PRICING/BUDGET, TIMING/URGENCY, COMPETITION, FEATURE-GAPS, AUTHORITY/DECISION-PROCESS, SECURITY/LEGAL/COMPLIANCE, INTEGRATION/TECHNICAL, ROI/PROOF. For each, record the category, the rep, the call id, and a paraphrase of what the prospect said. (3) Score the rep's response per objection: Effective (3), Partial (2), Ineffective (1). (4) For each category, extract the top-scoring rebuttal as a reusable template (the exact language the rep used and the result). (5) Compare this week's frequency by category to the prior 7-day window: flag rising, declining, and new categories. (6) Correlate categories with outcomes; flag the categories most tied to calls with no next step set as high-risk. If no objections at all, output exactly: 'No prospect objections detected in [n] calls this week. This may indicate early-stage pipeline or insufficient sample size.' and stop. Output the exact report format in objection-drilldown.md -> Output. Apply humanizer rules: no em dashes, no AI throat-clearing, no hype, one clear ask.

nextAction.name: post_report
nextAction.displayName: Post the report to the team channel
